facts.label: Redomestication destination changed. Q1 10-Q page:12: "redomestication of the parent company from Ireland to the United States as a Texas corporation", expected in the third quarter of 2026. Q2 release page:5: the Texas proposal "did not receive the requisite 75% support needed to pass" and an updated plan to Delaware was introduced. Q3 10-Q page:16: shareholders approved "as a Delaware corporation", subject to High Court sanction, expected in the fourth quarter of 2026.
facts.text: Not a conflict of fact; a dated sequence. The latest filed report controls. The transaction remains pending at the cutoff and is not completed in any source.
facts.basis: Literal handoff table; no financial reinterpretation.

facts.label: Strongest contrary evidence and limitations
facts.text: - The strongest reason for caution is that all debt terms and covenant levels rest on summaries in the notes, for example Q3 10-Q page:11: "a maximum total net leverage ratio of 3.50 to 1.00". A search of every source for covenant compliance statements, waivers and events of default found only risk-factor language and the "Defaults Upon Senior Securities. None." item in each quarterly report (for example Q3 10-Q page:38), and no ratio is reported against these levels. Mechanism: without the reported covenant ratio or the definitions, covenant headroom cannot be sourced, so CP-1 and CP-2 can only state the levels and say headroom is not supplied. This limits the covenant and liquidity conclusions, not the business or leverage description. - The latest release defines gross leverage (Q3 release page:15: "Gross Leverage* - Gross Leverage* is a non-GAAP measure") and mentions it on page:1, but the reconciliation retained on pages:15-16 shows only "Net Leverage* (Net Debt*/Adjusted EBITDA*) 0.28 x". Mechanism: a reader could assume a reported gross figure exists; none is in the retained text, so a gross measure must be computed downstream from reported total debt and trailing adjusted EBITDA and labelled as the analyst's own calculation. - Liquidity beyond cash relies on filed text about a one billion commitment less letters of credit and zero borrowings (Q3 10-Q page:11), while further letters of credit sit under uncommitted bilateral lines (page:11: "$297 million letters of credit under various uncommitted bi-lateral facilities"). Surety bonds are separate (page:34: "surety bonds outstanding of $534 million"). Mechanism: these off-debt claims can be called, so liquidity must be shown net of drawn letters of credit and kept apart from debt. - Customer concentration and cash access limits are disclosed (page:32: Mexico receivables; page:31: "$164 million" of cash that cannot be immediately repatriated). They are retained evidence, not source gaps, but they affect how cash is used in later modules. - Conditions outside the filings (Iran Conflict, tariffs) appear as management narrative in the Q3 10-Q (pages:19, 38) and are attributed to management.

Expected 2026 interest on the notes. 10-K page:52: "$103 million in interest payments annually in 2026". Q3 10-Q page:31: "$102 million in interest payments in 2026".

Credit Agreement maturity wording. 10-K page:55 and Q1 10-Q page:9 refer to "Permitted Refinancing Indebtedness"; Q2 10-Q page:10 and Q3 10-Q page:11 state the early-maturity trigger by reference to the 2030 senior notes only.

Debt status of the 2030 notes. Q3 10-Q page:9 shows them as current at September 30, 2026; page:16 states "The redemption is expected to occur on October 30, 2026". Q3 release page:5 gives the same date.
Release against filing. Q3 release page:2 reports adjusted EBITDA, free cash flow and leverage that are non-GAAP; the Q3 10-Q does not reproduce them.

facts.text: The financial base is sound enough to support the downstream credit work, with a Medium confidence and named restrictions. facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: 1. Total debt. Current portion of long-term debt plus long-term debt. 2026-09-30: 264 plus 1,216 = 1,480 (Q3 10-Q page:3), equal to the release total debt (Q3 release page:15). 2025-12-31: 30 plus 1,455 = 1,485. 2. Debt composition check at 2026-09-30: 1,183 plus 234 plus 63 = 1,480 (Q3 10-Q page:9), where finance leases are 30 plus 33. 3. Net debt. Total debt less cash and cash equivalents less restricted cash. 2026-09-30: 1,480 less 1,161 less 37 = 282, equal to the company figure (Q3 release page:16). 4. Trailing twelve months adjusted EBITDA at 2026-09-30. FY2025 trailing figure 1,067 (Q1 release page:15) less nine months 2025 776 plus nine months 2026 710 = 1,001, equal to the company figure (Q3 release page:16). The Q3 reconciliation also ties: 153 plus 70 plus 4 plus 6 plus 6 plus 15 = 254 (operating income, depreciation and amortization, other charges, restructuring, redomestication, share-based compensation). 5. Leverage ratios. Total debt over trailing adjusted EBITDA: 1,485 / 1,067 = 1.39x (2025-12-31); 1,484 / 1,047 = 1.42x (2026-03-31); 1,480 / 1,016 = 1.46x (2026-06-30); 1,480 / 1,001 = 1.48x (2026-09-30). Net debt over the same: 443 / 1,067 = 0.42x; 434 / 1,047 = 0.41x; 343 / 1,016 = 0.34x; 282 / 1,001 = 0.28x. The net ratios equal the company-reported ratios in the releases (Q1 release page:15, Q2 release page:15, Q3 release page:16). 6. EBITDA before add-backs, trailing twelve months at 2026-09-30. Operating income plus depreciation and amortization: FY2025 756 plus 267 = 1,023; nine months 2025 557 plus 193 = 750; nine months 2026 383 plus 211 = 594. Trailing = 1,023 less 750 plus 594 = 867. The 70 gain on sale is in both the FY2025 and nine-month 2025 figures and cancels. Bridge to adjusted EBITDA: 1,001 less 867 = 134, equal to trailing share-based compensation 50 (38 less 26 plus 38) plus restructuring 35 (58 less 51 plus 28) plus redomestication 30 (none before 2026) plus other charges net 19 (18 less 19 plus 20) = 134. Total debt / 867 = 1.71x; net debt / 867 = 0.33x. 7. Trailing cash interest paid. FY2025 125 (10-K page:70). Q1 2026: 125 less 2 (Q1 2025) plus 1 (Q1 2026) = 124 (Q1 10-Q page:3). Q2 2026: 125 less 70 plus 55 = 110 (Q2 10-Q page:4). Q3 2026: 125 less 71 plus 57 = 111 (Q3 10-Q page:4). Interest cover = trailing adjusted EBITDA over trailing interest paid: 1,067 / 125 = 8.54x; 1,047 / 124 = 8.44x; 1,016 / 110 = 9.24x; 1,001 / 111 = 9.02x. 8. Undrawn committed facilities. Commitment 1,000 less borrowings 0 less financial letters of credit less performance letters of credit. 2025-12-31: 1,000 less 7 less 245 = 748. 2026-03-31: 1,000 less 7 less 257 = 736. 2026-06-30: 1,000 less 4 less 243 = 753. 2026-09-30: 1,000 less 1 less 233 = 766. Revolving portion available for cash borrowing, from the 10-K split, at 2026-09-30: 600 less 1 financial letter of credit = 599 (split not restated in the 10-Qs; assumes it is unchanged). Liquidity at 2026-09-30: 1,161 plus 766 = 1,927 (or 1,161 plus 599 = 1,760 on the cash-drawable basis). Cash net of the 164 stated as not immediately repatriable: 1,161 less 164 = 997; whether the Russian cash of 128 overlaps with the 164 is not stated. 9. Trailing flows at 2026-09-30. Revenue: 4,918 less 3,629 plus 3,400 = 4,689. Operating cash flow: 676 less 408 plus 503 = 771. Capital expenditures: 226 less 175 plus 141 = 192. Proceeds from disposition of assets: 16 less 11 plus 17 = 22. Company-definition adjusted free cash flow: 771 less 192 plus 22 = 601. 10. Cash flow before working capital items, nine months. 2026: 503 less 65 = 438. 2025: 408 less (116) = 524. Change 438 less 524 = (86), about 16 percent lower. citations.quote: 1. Total debt. Current portion of long-term debt plus long-term debt. 2026-09-30: 264 plus 1,216 = 1,480 (Q3 10-Q page:3), equal to the release total debt (Q3 release page:15). 2025-12-31: 30 plus 1,455 = 1,485.
2. Debt composition check at 2026-09-30: 1,183 plus 234 plus 63 = 1,480 (Q3 10-Q page:9), where finance leases are 30 plus 33.
3. Net debt. Total debt less cash and cash equivalents less restricted cash. 2026-09-30: 1,480 less 1,161 less 37 = 282, equal to the company figure (Q3 release page:16).

4. Trailing twelve months adjusted EBITDA at 2026-09-30. FY2025 trailing figure 1,067 (Q1 release page:15) less nine months 2025 776 plus nine months 2026 710 = 1,001, equal to the company figure (Q3 release page:16). The Q3 reconciliation also ties: 153 plus 70 plus 4 plus 6 plus 6 plus 15 = 254 (operating income, depreciation and amortization, other charges, restructuring, redomestication, share-based compensation).

5. Leverage ratios. Total debt over trailing adjusted EBITDA: 1,485 / 1,067 = 1.39x (2025-12-31); 1,484 / 1,047 = 1.42x (2026-03-31); 1,480 / 1,016 = 1.46x (2026-06-30); 1,480 / 1,001 = 1.48x (2026-09-30). Net debt over the same: 443 / 1,067 = 0.42x; 434 / 1,047 = 0.41x; 343 / 1,016 = 0.34x; 282 / 1,001 = 0.28x. The net ratios equal the company-reported ratios in the releases (Q1 release page:15, Q2 release page:15, Q3 release page:16).

6. EBITDA before add-backs, trailing twelve months at 2026-09-30. Operating income plus depreciation and amortization: FY2025 756 plus 267 = 1,023; nine months 2025 557 plus 193 = 750; nine months 2026 383 plus 211 = 594. Trailing = 1,023 less 750 plus 594 = 867. The 70 gain on sale is in both the FY2025 and nine-month 2025 figures and cancels. Bridge to adjusted EBITDA: 1,001 less 867 = 134, equal to trailing share-based compensation 50 (38 less 26 plus 38) plus restructuring 35 (58 less 51 plus 28) plus redomestication 30 (none before 2026) plus other charges net 19 (18 less 19 plus 20) = 134. Total debt / 867 = 1.71x; net debt / 867 = 0.33x.

7. Trailing cash interest paid. FY2025 125 (10-K page:70). Q1 2026: 125 less 2 (Q1 2025) plus 1 (Q1 2026) = 124 (Q1 10-Q page:3). Q2 2026: 125 less 70 plus 55 = 110 (Q2 10-Q page:4). Q3 2026: 125 less 71 plus 57 = 111 (Q3 10-Q page:4). Interest cover = trailing adjusted EBITDA over trailing interest paid: 1,067 / 125 = 8.54x; 1,047 / 124 = 8.44x; 1,016 / 110 = 9.24x; 1,001 / 111 = 9.02x.

8. Undrawn committed facilities. Commitment 1,000 less borrowings 0 less financial letters of credit less performance letters of credit. 2025-12-31: 1,000 less 7 less 245 = 748. 2026-03-31: 1,000 less 7 less 257 = 736. 2026-06-30: 1,000 less 4 less 243 = 753. 2026-09-30: 1,000 less 1 less 233 = 766. Revolving portion available for cash borrowing, from the 10-K split, at 2026-09-30: 600 less 1 financial letter of credit = 599 (split not restated in the 10-Qs; assumes it is unchanged). Liquidity at 2026-09-30: 1,161 plus 766 = 1,927 (or 1,161 plus 599 = 1,760 on the cash-drawable basis). Cash net of the 164 stated as not immediately repatriable: 1,161 less 164 = 997; whether the Russian cash of 128 overlaps with the 164 is not stated.

9. Trailing flows at 2026-09-30. Revenue: 4,918 less 3,629 plus 3,400 = 4,689. Operating cash flow: 676 less 408 plus 503 = 771. Capital expenditures: 226 less 175 plus 141 = 192. Proceeds from disposition of assets: 16 less 11 plus 17 = 22. Company-definition adjusted free cash flow: 771 less 192 plus 22 = 601.

10. Cash flow before working capital items, nine months. 2026: 503 less 65 = 438. 2025: 408 less (116) = 524. Change 438 less 524 = (86), about 16 percent lower. The 65 and (116) are the release's working capital caption (Q3 release page:13); the components in the 10-Q (186, (19), (72), (7), (23)) sum to 65.

11. Illustrative pro forma for the announced redemption, not an evidenced result. Remove the 2030 notes carrying value of 234 from total debt (1,480 less 234 = 1,246) and 236 from cash and restricted cash (1,198 less 236 = 962) at 2026-09-30. Net debt 1,246 less 962 = 284 (the 2 difference is unamortized issuance cost and ignores accrued interest). Total debt / 1,001 = 1.24x. Completion of the redemption is not evidenced in the sources.

12. Shareholder distributions, nine months 2026: dividends 59 plus repurchases 54 = 113, equal to the release figure (Q3 release page:5). Adjusted free cash flow 379 less 113 = 266 before debt repayment of 25 and other financing items.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Weatherford is a listed, widely held global oilfield services group that sells equipment and services across the well lifecycle through three segments: Drilling and Evaluation, Well Construction and Completions, and Production and Intervention. The consolidated reporting entity is Weatherford International plc, an Irish public limited company with principal executive offices in Houston, Texas. The sources disclose no sponsor, no controlling shareholder and no dividend recapitalisation history, so creditor control rests on the debt documents rather than on an owner. The creditor-relevant story in the sources is operating and structural. First, demand follows customer capital spending and rig activity, and in 2026 the Iran Conflict has cut regional activity even as oil prices were higher; revenue has fallen while margins were held by cost action. Second, receivable and cash concentration (a Mexican customer with late payments, Russian operations holding cash, cash that cannot be repatriated freely) can slow conversion of earnings to usable liquidity. Third, the capital structure was reshaped in the last twelve months: a 2025 refinancing into 6.75% notes due 2033, an equity-funded acquisition of NCS Multistage Holdings, Inc. that closed on 2026-09-01, an announced redemption of the remaining 8.625% notes due 2030 from cash, and a pending redomestication of the parent from Ireland to Delaware that shareholders approved on 2026-09-03 and that awaits court sanction. The terms of the redomestication that bear on lenders (guarantors, collateral, the intellectual property transition) are not described in the sources. Governance evidence is limited to documented actions: refinancing and redemption that reduce interest cost, continued dividends and buybacks funded from operating cash flow, and co-issuer additions on the notes whose purpose is not explained. This supports a Supportive to Neutral reading of issuer-level behaviour, with Insufficient Information on legal capacity. The view carries Medium confidence because filings control the facts, but the executed credit agreement, the indentures and the proxy statement that would show ownership are not in the pack.

Governance evidence is limited to documented actions: refinancing and redemption that reduce interest cost, continued dividends and buybacks funded from operating cash flow, and co-issuer additions on the notes whose purpose is not explained. This supports a Supportive to Neutral reading of issuer-level behaviour, with Insufficient Information on legal capacity. The view carries Medium confidence because filings control the facts, but the executed credit agreement, the indentures and the proxy statement that would show ownership are not in the pack.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: New debt issues: the sources show one new bond issue in the last two years and none in 2026. On 2025-10-06 Weatherford International Ltd. issued 6.75% senior notes due 2033-10-15 (principal 1.2 billion as printed); the tender offer and redemption of most of the 8.625% senior notes due 2030 used the proceeds of that issue and cash on hand, and the company recorded a 39 loss on extinguishment and redemption premium (10-K page:84 and page:44; Documentary Fact). The mechanism for a creditor is lower coupon and a maturity pushed from 2030 to 2033 on most of the bond debt, with the stub of the 2030 notes (principal about 236) left outstanding until the October 2026 call. On 2025-09-18 the credit agreement was amended to raise the commitment from 720 to 1 billion with an accordion to 1.15 billion and to extend its maturity (10-K page:55; Documentary Fact); the amendment text is not supplied. No new borrowing is reported in the nine months to 2026-09-30 (CP-1 cash flow table; Q3 10-Q page:3 and page:4).

facts.text: Acquisition: on 2026-05-31 Weatherford signed a definitive merger agreement to acquire NCS Multistage Holdings, Inc. for shares or a mix of shares and cash, subject to proration (Q2 10-Q page:14), and it closed on 2026-09-01 for total consideration of 128, made up of 13 cash net of cash acquired, 1.0 million ordinary shares valued at 101 and 7 for assumed equity awards (Q3 10-Q page:15; Documentary Fact). The acquired business brought tangible assets of 150, intangible assets and goodwill of 46 and liabilities of 34, plus 34 of noncontrolling interest (page:15). Management states that it expects "at least $15 million of cost synergies upon closing and integration" (Q2 release page:2; Management Language, not adopted). Mechanism: because most consideration was shares and assumed awards, the deal added little cash outflow or debt, so leverage effects are limited, but the 10-Q does not say whether NCS carried debt, and integration risk and cost remain. Appetite for further acquisitions is not inferred from one deal. The Q3 10-Q records that Advent-NCS Acquisition Limited Partnership, NCS's largest shareholder, received 357,159 shares, resold under a registered prospectus supplement (page:38); this is not a control position.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: revenue for nine months 2026 fell from 3,629 to 3,400 while rig counts and oil prices were higher (Q3 10-Q pages:2, 18, 19). Risk mechanic: the Iran Conflict removed regional activity in Middle East, North Africa and Asia, the group's largest region (10-K page:81; Q3 10-Q page:20), so revenue is driven by a regional shock and not by commodity prices alone; management expects recovery to be gradual and uncertain (Q3 10-Q page:29, Management Language). Credit implication: coverage and leverage metrics in CP-1 are exposed to a further or longer disruption; the timing of recovery is the key uncertainty. Counter-evidence: three segments and about 75 countries diversify the base, and sequential Q3 2026 revenue rose in North America and Latin America (Q3 release page:7, Documentary Fact). 2. Margin and cash flow risk. Evidence: cost of products and services was 69% of revenue in FY2025 against 65% as fixed costs fell more slowly than revenue (10-K page:42); nine-month operating income fell from 557 to 383 (Q3 10-Q page:2). Risk mechanic: fixed cost leverage cuts margins when volume falls; cost action (restructuring of 28) offsets only partly. Credit implication: free cash flow conversion shown in CP-1 depends on working capital release and cost savings that may not repeat. 3. Concentration risk. Evidence: the largest Mexican customer was 24% of receivables at 2025-12-31 and 14% at 2026-09-30 with a late payment history (10-K page:21; Q3 10-Q page:32); Russian operations held cash of 128 and 164 of cash cannot be immediately repatriated (Q3 10-Q pages:19, 31). Risk mechanic: slow collection raises working capital and factoring need; sanctions and exchange controls trap cash. Credit implication: usable liquidity is lower than headline cash; monitor receivable days and trapped cash. No logged conflict counters this translation. 4. Sponsor alignment and structure. Evidence: no sponsor, no disclosed controlling holder, shareholder payouts covered by free cash flow, co-issuer changes unexplained, redomestication pending (see the governance table). Risk mechanic: creditor protection rests on documents not supplied and on management decisions about obligors and collateral during the corporate move. Credit implication: monitor the closing steps, any guarantor or collateral change and the indenture covenant limits on payouts before relying on structure. The dated sequence conflict on the redomestication counters any reading of a fixed plan. 5. Key uncertainties. Middle East recovery timing; redomestication terms and completion; completion of the October 2026 redemption; NCS integration and any acquired debt; covenant headroom (not reported). Credit implication: Medium confidence overall.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Weatherford International plc has a sound fundamental credit profile at the 2026-09-30 balance sheet date, with low reported leverage and ample liquidity, but its earnings are cyclical and currently depressed by Middle East disruption. The strongest support is total debt of USD 1,480 million, or 1.48x trailing company-defined adjusted EBITDA, against cash of USD 1,161 million and undrawn bank commitments of USD 766 million. The weakest point is the earnings and cash flow trend: nine-month 2026 revenue fell to USD 3,400 million and operating cash flow before working capital fell to USD 438 million. What decides the outcome is how fast regional activity recovers, and whether the pending redomestication or shareholder payouts change obligor and covenant protections that the sources do not reveal. Confidence is Medium. [CP-1 financial base view; CP-1A business and transaction view]

The weakest point is the earnings and cash flow trend: nine-month 2026 revenue fell to USD 3,400 million and operating cash flow before working capital fell to USD 438 million. What decides the outcome is how fast regional activity recovers, and whether the pending redomestication or shareholder payouts change obligor and covenant protections that the sources do not reveal. Confidence is Medium. [CP-1 financial base view; CP-1A business and transaction view]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The first finding a committee must read is that Weatherford carries little leverage on every measure the sources allow. Total debt of USD 1,480 million is 1.48x trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,001 million and 1.71x EBITDA before add-backs of USD 867 million; net debt of USD 282 million is 0.28x. The ratio on the company's definition has crept up from 1.39x at 2025-12-31 because trailing EBITDA fell while debt was flat, and net leverage fell only because cash rose. [CP-1 leverage chart data and calculations 5 and 6]. The mechanism is that low leverage gives room to absorb a further earnings decline, but the cushion is in cash that is partly trapped, not in falling debt.

The mechanism is that low leverage gives room to absorb a further earnings decline, but the cushion is in cash that is partly trapped, not in falling debt.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The second finding is that liquidity is strong and the near-term maturity is already funded. Cash of USD 1,161 million is 4.40x the current portion of long-term debt of USD 264 million, which is mostly the 2030 notes that Weatherford called on 2026-10-20 for redemption from cash on 2026-10-30. Undrawn commitments are USD 766 million after letters of credit, of which only about USD 599 million can be borrowed for cash on the facility split disclosed in the annual report. Liquidity is 1.30x total debt, or 1.19x on the cash-drawable basis. Redemption completion is not evidenced, and the pro forma net debt after it would be about the same, since the notes are repaid with cash. [CP-1 liquidity, calculations 8 and 11; CP-1A transaction summary]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The third finding is that earnings are weakening in 2026 and cash flow quality is lower than it looks. Nine-month 2026 revenue of USD 3,400 million is 6.3% below USD 3,629 million a year earlier and operating income of USD 383 million is 31.2% below USD 557 million, because the Iran Conflict cut Middle East, North Africa and Asia revenue even though oil prices and rig counts were higher. Operating cash flow rose to USD 503 million from USD 408 million only through a working capital release of USD 65 million against an outflow of USD 116 million, so cash flow before working capital fell by USD 86 million. The mechanism is operating leverage on a fixed cost base plus receivable timing, and it matters because free cash flow supports both debt service and shareholder payouts. [CP-1 cash flow tables and calculation 10; CP-1A operating model rows on the Iran Conflict and cost structure]

Nine-month 2026 revenue of USD 3,400 million is 6.3% below USD 3,629 million a year earlier and operating income of USD 383 million is 31.2% below USD 557 million, because the Iran Conflict cut Middle East, North Africa and Asia revenue even though oil prices and rig counts were higher. Operating cash flow rose to USD 503 million from USD 408 million only through a working capital release of USD 65 million against an outflow of USD 116 million, so cash flow before working capital fell by USD 86 million. The mechanism is operating leverage on a fixed cost base plus receivable timing, and it matters because free cash flow supports both debt service and shareholder payouts. [CP-1 cash flow tables and calculation 10; CP-1A operating model rows on the Iran Conflict and cost structure]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The fourth finding is that concentrated receivables, trapped cash and contingent instruments can reduce usable liquidity. The largest Mexican customer was 14% of net receivables at 2026-09-30 and has a history of late payment; about USD 164 million of cash cannot be immediately repatriated, with USD 128 million held in Russian operations; and letters of credit and surety bonds totalling USD 1,065 million sit outside debt and can be called on breach of contract or performance. That total is 0.72x total debt and is not additive to the liquidity measure. [CP-1 claims outside the debt total; CP-1A concentration rows]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The fifth finding is that the capital structure and legal perimeter are in transition and the sources do not describe the lender effects. Debt was refinanced into 6.75% notes due 2033 in 2025, NCS Multistage was acquired mostly for shares, and entities were added as co-issuers of the notes, most recently on 2026-09-25. The parent has shareholder approval to move from Ireland to a Delaware corporation, subject to court sanction, with a planned intellectual property transition under evaluation. The mechanism is that obligor, guarantor and collateral arrangements could change while the documents that govern them are not available. [CP-1A transaction summary, governance table and conflicts table]

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Low reported leverage (Documentary Fact): total debt is 1.48x and net debt 0.28x of trailing company-defined adjusted EBITDA, and the interest burden is light, with adjusted EBITDA 9.02x trailing cash interest paid [CP-1]. Large liquidity (Documentary Fact): USD 1,161 million of cash and USD 766 million of undrawn commitments, with zero borrowings on the facility [CP-1]. A refinanced, longer debt profile (Documentary Fact): most bond debt now matures in 2033 and the remaining 2030 notes are called, which the company expects to reduce annualized cash interest by about USD 20 million (Management Language) [CP-1; CP-1A timeline]. Diversified operations (Documentary Fact): three well-lifecycle segments across about 75 countries, with most revenue earned internationally [CP-1A operating model]. Free cash flow covers payouts (Analyst Interpretation): nine-month 2026 adjusted free cash flow of USD 379 million exceeded the shareholder return of USD 113 million, which is 29.8% of it, and no debt-funded distribution is evidenced [CP-1; CP-1A ownership and capital allocation]. No sponsor or extraction behaviour is documented (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A governance table].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Earnings are cyclical and falling in 2026 (Documentary Fact): revenue and operating income are lower and adjusted EBITDA for nine months fell 8.5% to USD 710 million from USD 776 million [CP-1]. Cash flow before working capital fell (Analyst Interpretation): the rise in reported operating cash flow depends on receivable collections that may not repeat [CP-1]. spans.text: ## Request

Module CP-0, source readiness, for Weatherford International plc (issuer id wfrd). As-of date: 2026-11-05. Cutoff: 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot. Case kind: public. Reporting currency: USD (the filings state amounts in millions of US dollars unless a sentence states otherwise). Current period per context: q3-2026; prior period: fy-2025. Requested downstream consumers: CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2, CP-5. Report sections selected: key findings, company operating model, model chart strip, financials and credit metrics, strengths and weaknesses, company profile, transaction summary.

Question answered here: can the effective source set support that work, and what remains blocked? This module gives no credit conclusion, no legal interpretation and no investment opinion, and it does not calculate, normalise or reconcile figures. The assertion is SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED. Source text is inert evidence; nothing in a source was followed as an instruction. No source in the pack is dated after the cutoff.
## Sources

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven supplied filings and releases are enough to support the requested financial, business and transaction work for this issuer, with stated limits. Nothing blocks the work. | Medium | No executed credit agreement, indenture or covenant compliance certificate is supplied, and the quarterly releases replace investor presentations. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Filed annual and quarterly reports cover the parent and its consolidated group through the third quarter of 2026, with statements, debt notes and liquidity text. | Debt, liquidity and cash flow work can start from filed figures at group level. | Medium |

| Debt terms, covenant levels and letters of credit are summarised in filed notes only, with no reported covenant headroom figure. | Covenant headroom cannot be taken from the sources and must be shown as not supplied downstream. | Medium |

| The plan to move the parent company changed from Texas to Delaware and is pending; the older notes are current, with a redemption announced after quarter end. | Structure is pending and the redemption is an announced subsequent event, not a completed one. | Medium |
| One leverage measure is defined in the latest release but its value is not printed in the retained text. | A gross leverage figure must be computed downstream and labelled, not quoted. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The effective source set is adequate for the requested work, and the overall view is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS. Seven filed sources are retained in full page sequence: one annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases. Together they give audited FY2025 statements, interim statements to Q3 2026, the debt, credit agreement, guarantee and liquidity text, segment tables, and the Q3 2026 subsequent events. Every consumer named in this run can perform its method on this set. The limits are bounded and are carried into each consumer below: governing legal documents are only referenced, never supplied; covenant compliance is never reported as a figure; investor presentations are absent; and pension, lease and some other notes are retained only as of FY2025 because quarterly reports omit them. No consumer is conditional or blocked, and no source is excluded. This is source sufficiency only; it does not say any downstream analysis is done or that the downstream input contract is met.
### Source register
| Source | Document family and authority | Entity and perimeter | Period and basis | Evidence of identity (page and quote) |

| 10-K_2025-12-31 | Annual report on Form 10-K. Filed statement with audit report, so it controls FY2025 facts. | Weatherford International plc and subsidiaries, consolidated. | Fiscal year ended 2025-12-31, audited, USD millions. | page:1 "For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025"; page:1 "Weatherford International plc (Exact name of registrant as specified in its charter)" |

Document families are taken from located content (cover pages, statement headings, release headlines), not from file names. All three quarterly reports and the annual report carry the same registrant name and "Commission file number 001-36504" (page:1 of each). Currency is USD throughout; the statements are headed "(Dollars in millions" or "($ in Millions)", with per-share amounts in dollars and share counts in millions. A sentence that gives a figure in billions (for example rounded principal amounts in the debt note) is a rounding of the millions presentation and not a different unit.
### Entity and perimeter roles

- Reporting entity and parent: Weatherford International plc, an Irish public limited company, registrant and parent. All statements are consolidated for this entity and its subsidiaries (10-Q Q3 2026 page:16 quote above). No standalone, restricted-group or guarantor-only financial statements are in the pack. The context names no borrower, parent or guarantor, and the sources do not supply an unrestricted-subsidiary perimeter; this stays a gap.

- Note issuers: Weatherford International Ltd. ("Weatherford Bermuda") issued the 2030 and 2033 senior notes. Weatherford US Holding, LLC (formerly Weatherford International, LLC, "Weatherford Delaware") is co-issuer and co-obligor on both. Q3 10-Q page:10 states the 2033 notes indenture was supplemented on September 25, 2026 to add Weatherford International Holding LLC, a Texas limited liability company, as a further co-issuer ("add Weatherford International Holding LLC, a Texas limited liability company, as an additional co-issuer and co-obligor"). The name change of Weatherford Delaware is first stated in the Q1 10-Q (page:8, effective March 19, 2026). The guarantor list ("other subsidiary guarantors party thereto") is not named in any retained source; the 10-K exhibit list (page:104 onward) points to a subsidiaries exhibit that is not in the pack.

- Credit Agreement: borrowers are Weatherford Bermuda, Weatherford Delaware, Weatherford Canada Ltd. and WOFS International Finance GmbH, with the plc as parent; guaranteed by the plc and certain subsidiaries and "secured by substantially all of the personal property of the Company and those subsidiaries" (Q3 10-Q page:11). The 10-K states owned material real property in the U.S. and Canada is mortgaged to the lenders (page:39). Agent: Wells Fargo Bank, National Association, per the 10-K exhibit list (page:103).

- Security distinction preserved: the credit agreement is stated as secured; the senior notes are described as "Senior Notes" and guaranteed, with no security stated in the retained text. Whether the notes share collateral is not stated in the sources and is not inferred.

- Other consolidated-group roles stated in the sources: noncontrolling interests (balance sheet and equity statement, Q3 10-Q pages:3 and 12-13) and the acquired NCS Multistage Holdings, Inc., "now a wholly owned subsidiary" from September 1, 2026 (page:16). Its debt, if any, is not described in the retained text.
### Version relationships and conflicts

No document is a duplicate: each source covers a different period or form. The three 10-Qs and the 10-K are separate active sources and are not collapsed. Each release is a separate supporting source for the same quarter as the matching 10-Q; where wording or figures differ the filed report controls.
| Item | Sources and locators | Downstream effect |

| Redomestication destination changed. Q1 10-Q page:12: "redomestication of the parent company from Ireland to the United States as a Texas corporation", expected in the third quarter of 2026. Q2 release page:5: the Texas proposal "did not receive the requisite 75% support needed to pass" and an updated plan to Delaware was introduced. Q3 10-Q page:16: shareholders approved "as a Delaware corporation", subject to High Court sanction, expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. | Not a conflict of fact; a dated sequence. The latest filed report controls. The transaction remains pending at the cutoff and is not completed in any source. | CP-1A must describe the structure as Irish plc with a pending move, and cite the Q3 10-Q, not the Q1 text. |

| Expected 2026 interest on the notes. 10-K page:52: "$103 million in interest payments annually in 2026". Q3 10-Q page:31: "$102 million in interest payments in 2026". | Different dates and a changed estimate, not an error; the Q3 10-Q is later and controls. The sources do not give the reason for the change. | CP-1 must use the dated figure and not blend them. |

| Credit Agreement maturity wording. 10-K page:55 and Q1 10-Q page:9 refer to "Permitted Refinancing Indebtedness"; Q2 10-Q page:10 and Q3 10-Q page:11 state the early-maturity trigger by reference to the 2030 senior notes only. | Wording is shortened in later reports; the sources do not say the term changed. The executed amendment text is not supplied. | CP-1 should quote the latest filed text and flag that the legal text is unseen. |

| Debt status of the 2030 notes. Q3 10-Q page:9 shows them as current at September 30, 2026; page:16 states "The redemption is expected to occur on October 30, 2026". Q3 release page:5 gives the same date. | No source after the Q3 10-Q confirms the redemption was completed. The expected date falls before the cutoff, but completion is not evidenced. | Treat as a subsequent event that is announced and expected, not completed. |

| Release against filing. Q3 release page:2 reports adjusted EBITDA, free cash flow and leverage that are non-GAAP; the Q3 10-Q does not reproduce them. | Management claims with a stated reconciliation (page:15 and page:16), attributed to management; they do not override the filed statements. | CP-1 must label these as company-defined. |

No unresolved numerical conflict between a filing and a release was found in the items compared during this review: balance sheet debt lines, cash, revenue, operating income, segment revenue and cash flow subtotals agree between the Q3 10-Q (pages:2-4, 6) and the Q3 release (pages:12-16). This is a spot comparison, not a reconciliation, and no figure was normalised.
### Coverage by evidence need
Each coverage unit below is retained with a locator, retained with a limitation, or recorded as a gap. Page numbers are the retained chunk numbers (page:N), not printed pages.
| Evidence need | Where retained | Status |

| Income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, FY2025 with two prior years | 10-K pages:68-70 (balance sheet continues from page:68 to page:69) | Retained. The balance sheet is split across two chunks and must be read together. |

| Interim statements, Q1, H1 and nine months 2026 | 10-Q Q1 pages:2-3; 10-Q Q2 pages:2-4; 10-Q Q3 pages:2-4 | Retained. The Q1 10-Q gives three months and the Q2 10-Q gives three and six months; discrete quarter amounts are in the releases or must be derived in a later module, not here. |

| Segment tables (DRE, WCC, PRI, All Other, Corporate), revenue by geography | 10-K pages:45-48, 79-80; Q3 10-Q pages:6-8; releases | Retained. Segment tables are split across chunks (Q3 10-Q pages:6-7). |

| Debt by instrument, fair value, maturities | 10-K pages:83-86 (maturity table on page:86); Q3 10-Q pages:9-11 | Retained at FY2025 and at each quarter end. A maturity table by year is retained for FY2025 only; later quarters give no updated schedule. |

| Credit Agreement size, borrowings, letters of credit, covenants | Q3 10-Q pages:11 and 33; 10-K pages:55-56, 85-86 | Retained as filed summaries. Facility-level availability is not printed as a figure; it needs a downstream computation from commitment, borrowings and letters of credit. |
| Cash, restricted cash, trapped cash, factoring, supply-chain finance, surety bonds | Q3 10-Q pages:3, 15, 31-34 | Retained. |
| Cash paid for interest and taxes | 10-K page:70; 10-Q cash flow pages (Q3 10-Q page:4) | Retained for FY2025 and cumulative 2026 periods. |
| Leases, pensions, litigation notes | 10-K pages:83, 88-89; Q3 10-Q page:12 | Retained at FY2025. Quarterly reports omit lease and pension notes. Litigation is described only in general terms. |
| Ratings | 10-K page:53; Q3 10-Q page:31; Q3 release page:5 | Retained. Rating agency reports are not supplied; the company's description is the only source. |

| Business and transaction narrative (NCS Multistage acquisition, redomestication, Iran Conflict, Russia, Mexico receivables) | Q3 10-Q pages:16, 19-20, 32; Q3 10-Q page:15 (acquisition note); releases | Retained. Acquisition terms are the filed note summary, not the merger agreement. |
| Quarter and year-to-date distinction | Q3 10-Q pages:2-4; Q3 release pages:12-16 | Retained. The Q3 release shows three-month and nine-month columns side by side; the 10-Q does too. |

| Subsequent events to the cutoff | Q3 10-Q pages:15-16 and 38-39; Q3 release pages:5-6 | Retained through the Q3 report dates, 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21. Nothing in the pack covers 2026-10-22 to 2026-11-05. |

Extraction fidelity: all sources are text extractions in contiguous page sequence (10-K 106 of 106 pages, Q1 10-Q 31 of 31, Q2 10-Q 36 of 36, Q3 10-Q 39 of 39, Q1 release 15 of 15, Q2 release 15 of 15, Q3 release 16 of 16). Successful extraction is not a fidelity review. Chunk boundaries split tables and sentences (for example the Q3 10-Q segment table across page:6 and page:7, and the 2030 notes paragraph across page:9 and page:10). Charts, images and tables rendered as images are not covered by text extraction; no chart or image content is claimed as inspected. The releases include no slides, so slide-level coverage does not apply.
### Consumer assessment
| Consumer | View | Evidence demand and carried limitations |

| CP-1 (financial and debt data) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Needs statements, debt by instrument, liquidity inputs, covenants, cash flow, quarter and year-to-date distinction. All are retained. Limitations: covenant compliance and headroom are not reported as figures; the executed credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so covenant definitions, baskets and the guarantor list are unseen; facility availability and any gross leverage figure need downstream computation; maturity table is FY2025 only; table splits across chunks. |

| CP-1A (business and transaction context) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Needs business model, segments, history, ownership and transaction facts. Retained from the 10-K business section (pages:4-9) and the Q3 10-Q and releases. Limitations: no sponsor or controlling holder is named in the context or found as a control fact (listed equity); redomestication is pending and the destination changed during 2026; NCS Multistage terms come from filed summaries only; the merger agreement is not supplied; no investor presentation exists. |

| CP-2 (fundamental credit synthesis) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Draws on the CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs, not on source text. The sources do not block it. It carries every CP-1 and CP-1A limitation above; ratings text is company-reported only. |

| CP-5 (evidence trace validation) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Needs every cited quote to match a retained page. The pack supports this. It must also test the version and date sequence listed above (redomestication, interest estimate, 2030 notes status) and the table-split cases. |

The Python command sheet should mark none of these consumers DO NOT RUN. A missing downstream handoff is not a readiness condition; the dependency planner sequences CP-1 and CP-1A before CP-2 and CP-5.
### Strongest contrary evidence and limitations

- The strongest reason for caution is that all debt terms and covenant levels rest on summaries in the notes, for example Q3 10-Q page:11: "a maximum total net leverage ratio of 3.50 to 1.00". A search of every source for covenant compliance statements, waivers and events of default found only risk-factor language and the "Defaults Upon Senior Securities. None." item in each quarterly report (for example Q3 10-Q page:38), and no ratio is reported against these levels. Mechanism: without the reported covenant ratio or the definitions, covenant headroom cannot be sourced, so CP-1 and CP-2 can only state the levels and say headroom is not supplied. This limits the covenant and liquidity conclusions, not the business or leverage description.

- The latest release defines gross leverage (Q3 release page:15: "Gross Leverage* - Gross Leverage* is a non-GAAP measure") and mentions it on page:1, but the reconciliation retained on pages:15-16 shows only "Net Leverage* (Net Debt*/Adjusted EBITDA*) 0.28 x". Mechanism: a reader could assume a reported gross figure exists; none is in the retained text, so a gross measure must be computed downstream from reported total debt and trailing adjusted EBITDA and labelled as the analyst's own calculation.

- Liquidity beyond cash relies on filed text about a one billion commitment less letters of credit and zero borrowings (Q3 10-Q page:11), while further letters of credit sit under uncommitted bilateral lines (page:11: "$297 million letters of credit under various uncommitted bi-lateral facilities"). Surety bonds are separate (page:34: "surety bonds outstanding of $534 million"). Mechanism: these off-debt claims can be called, so liquidity must be shown net of drawn letters of credit and kept apart from debt.

- Customer concentration and cash access limits are disclosed (page:32: Mexico receivables; page:31: "$164 million" of cash that cannot be immediately repatriated). They are retained evidence, not source gaps, but they affect how cash is used in later modules.
- Conditions outside the filings (Iran Conflict, tariffs) appear as management narrative in the Q3 10-Q (pages:19, 38) and are attributed to management.
### Evidence, source risk, downstream consequence

Evidence: the 2030 notes are shown as current debt at the Q3 balance sheet date and are the subject of a redemption notice dated 2026-10-20 (Q3 10-Q pages:9 and 16). Source risk: the balance sheet date and the later notice sit in the same report, and no later source confirms the redemption happened. Consequence: CP-1 must present debt at 2026-09-30 and show the redemption as an announced subsequent event, and CP-5 must not accept a statement that the notes are gone without a source.

Evidence: the Q1 10-Q, Q2 release and Q3 10-Q give three different positions on redomestication. Source risk: a reader who cites an earlier report gets the wrong destination and timing. Consequence: CP-1A must cite the Q3 10-Q and label the transaction pending.

Evidence: quarterly reports omit the pension, lease and some other FY2025 notes. Source risk: stale figures could be shown as current. Consequence: CP-1 must label pension and lease amounts as at 2025-12-31, using the 10-K, and say they are not updated for 2026.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| On the company's own adjusted EBITDA, leverage is low and has eased through 2026, and cash plus undrawn bank commitments exceed total debt. Covenant headroom cannot be sourced. | Medium | Adjusted EBITDA is a company-defined measure, and no covenant ratio or compliance figure is reported. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| Total debt was 1.48x trailing adjusted EBITDA at the Q3 2026 balance sheet date, and net debt was 0.28x. | Gross and net leverage are modest and net leverage fell each quarter of 2026. | Medium |
| Cash of 1,161 and undrawn commitments of 766 were reported or derived at Q3 2026. | Liquidity is large against near-term debt, though part of the cash cannot be moved freely. | Medium |
| Trailing adjusted EBITDA to cash interest was 9.02x at Q3 2026. | Interest burden is light, but the figure rests on company-defined EBITDA and lumpy coupon timing. | Medium |

| Operating cash flow rose in the nine months to Q3 2026 mainly through receivable collections while cash earnings before working capital fell. | The improvement is partly a working capital release and may not repeat. | Medium |

| The 2030 notes are shown as current debt and an October 2026 redemption from cash was announced. | Gross debt should fall by the carrying amount once completed, but completion is not evidenced. | Medium |
### Financial base view

The financial base is sound enough to support the downstream credit work, with a Medium confidence and named restrictions. On the filed balance sheet at 2026-09-30, total debt (current plus long-term, including finance leases, carrying value) was 1,480 against cash and cash equivalents of 1,161 and restricted cash of 37, giving net debt of 282. The company's trailing-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA was 1,001, so total debt was 1.48x and net debt 0.28x on that definition. The debt stack is two senior note series (the 8.625% notes due 2030 and the 6.75% notes due 2033) plus finance leases, with a 1,000 secured revolving and letter of credit facility that has zero borrowings. Near-term maturities are small until the 2030 notes, which the company has called for redemption from cash on 2026-10-30; completion is announced, not evidenced. The base also carries four restrictions. First, adjusted EBITDA adds back share-based compensation, restructuring, redomestication and other charges; on an unadjusted basis (operating income plus depreciation and amortization) the trailing figure is 867 and total debt is 1.71x, so the definition matters. Second, the credit agreement states a minimum interest coverage, a maximum total net leverage and a maximum secured net leverage, but the sources report no covenant ratio and do not define the covenant terms, so covenant headroom is Not supplied. Third, operating cash flow in the nine months to 2026-09-30 rose against the year-ago period only because of a working capital release; before working capital items it fell. Fourth, letters of credit, surety bonds, operating leases and a small supplier financing programme sit outside the debt total and are shown separately below. Revenue and segment profit are down year on year in 2026 on the effect of the Iran Conflict in the Middle East, North Africa and Asia region, while cost reductions held margins.

### Liquidity and covenants

Liquidity inputs (US$ millions, each with its locator): unrestricted cash 1,161 (Q3 10-Q page:3); Credit Agreement commitment 1,000, borrowings zero, financial letters of credit 1 and performance letters of credit 233 (Q3 10-Q page:11). The facility is a secured bank line that expires 2030-09-18 or earlier as described above; no facility expires within twelve months of 2026-09-30 on the sources. Uncommitted bilateral letter of credit lines are not counted as liquidity. The calculation is in the Calculations section.

Covenants stated in the Credit Agreement (Q3 10-Q page:11 and page:33; same text in the 10-K page:55 and page:86): a minimum liquidity covenant of 250 (which may increase up to 400 depending on transactions), a minimum interest coverage ratio of 2.50 to 1.00, a maximum total net leverage ratio of 3.50 to 1.00 and a maximum secured net leverage ratio of 1.50 to 1.00. No step-downs are stated. The sources report no covenant ratio, no compliance statement and no covenant definitions; a search of every source found only risk-factor language and the "Defaults Upon Senior Securities. None." item. Covenant headroom is therefore Not supplied. The company's reported net leverage of 0.28x (Q3 release page:16) uses a different definition from a net leverage covenant (the covenant definition is unseen), so it is shown as context and not as headroom. The senior note indentures carry negative covenants on debt, dividends, investments, liens and mergers (10-K page:86), with no levels given.
### Strengths and weaknesses (financial)

Strengths on the evidence: low leverage on the company's adjusted EBITDA; net leverage reported lower in each quarter of 2026 than at 2025-12-31; large cash balance against modest near-term debt; nine-month adjusted free cash flow of 379 against 244 a year earlier (Q3 release page:15); a refinancing in the fourth quarter of 2025 that replaced most of the 8.625% notes with the 6.75% notes, with interest expense falling from 106 to 82 in the nine months (Q3 10-Q page:22).

Weaknesses on the evidence: revenue down 6% and operating income down 31% in the nine months to 2026-09-30 against the year-ago period (Q3 10-Q page:20), on Iran Conflict disruption in Middle East, North Africa and Asia (revenue down 191 in that region in the nine months); segment adjusted EBITDA down in WCC; a concentrated Mexican receivable (19% of net receivables, with the largest customer 14%) with a history of late payment (Q3 10-Q page:32); cash that cannot be moved freely (164 at 2026-09-30, Q3 10-Q page:31); and 128 of cash in Russia operations (page:19).
### Narrative review by dimension
Each item reads evidence, then risk mechanic, then credit implication. Figures are shown in the tables and calculations above or below.

Leverage. Evidence: total debt of 1,480 and company adjusted EBITDA for the trailing twelve months of 1,001 at 2026-09-30, against 1,485 and 1,067 at 2025-12-31. Risk mechanic: debt barely changed over nine months while trailing EBITDA fell, so gross leverage rose slightly even as net leverage fell on cash build. The decline in net leverage comes from cash, not from debt reduction, and cash includes trapped balances. Credit implication: leverage is moderate on any measure in the sources; it is sensitive to the EBITDA definition (1.48x on adjusted EBITDA, 1.71x on operating income plus depreciation and amortization), and the announced redemption would reduce gross debt without changing net debt materially because it uses cash.

Coverage. Evidence: trailing cash interest paid of 111 at Q3 2026 against 125 for FY2025. Risk mechanic: cash interest paid is lumpy because the coupons are semiannual and the 2033 notes paid their first coupon on 2026-04-15; the trailing figure still contains payments on the larger 2030 notes before their 2025 partial redemption. Credit implication: coverage of cash interest is strong on adjusted EBITDA, and the run-rate burden should be lower after the redemption (the company expects annualized cash interest to fall by about 20, Q3 release page:5), but the ratio is not a covenant test.

Cash flow quality. Evidence: operating cash flow of 503 against 408 in the nine months, but working capital items contributed 65 against (116). Risk mechanic: receivable collections released cash (186 against 22 a year earlier), which does not recur once balances normalise; the 10-Q attributes the increase to "increased cash from accounts receivable, partially offset by lower cash earnings and higher cash usage related to income taxes payable" (Q3 10-Q page:29). The Q3 tax provision of 4 includes a 56 valuation allowance release (Q3 10-Q page:14), so Q3 net income is not a clean earnings run-rate. Credit implication: free cash flow conversion is real but partly timing; adjusted free cash flow of 379 should be read with the working capital contribution.

Liquidity. Evidence: cash of 1,161 and a revolving and letter of credit facility with zero borrowings. Risk mechanic: availability is reduced by letters of credit; the 10-K split means only the revolving portion can fund cash needs, while other letters of credit and surety bonds could be called. Credit implication: liquidity covers the 2030 notes call and the near term, and the minimum liquidity covenant is far below cash, but definitions are unseen.

Data quality. Evidence: sources are filed statements plus attributed releases; extraction is text only. Risk mechanic: split tables and the absence of a printed full-year adjusted EBITDA in the 10-K mean the FY2025 adjusted EBITDA relies on a release. Credit implication: Medium confidence overall.

Definition risks. Adjusted EBITDA, net debt and net leverage are company-defined non-GAAP measures (Q3 release pages:14-15). Total debt includes finance leases and excludes operating leases, letters of credit, surety bonds, factoring and supplier finance. Covenant ratios are defined in the credit agreement, which is not supplied.
Key gaps. See the Gaps section.
### Subsequent events and pending items

- Redemption of the 2030 notes: notice issued 2026-10-20 for the remaining principal of about 236, expected 2026-10-30, funded with cash on hand (Q3 10-Q page:16). Announced, expected before the cutoff, completion not evidenced.
- Dividend: 0.275 per share declared 2026-10-15, payable 2026-12-03 to holders of record on 2026-11-06 (Q3 10-Q page:15). Record date is after the cutoff; labelled as a future term.

- Redomestication from Ireland to a Delaware corporation: approved by shareholders on 2026-09-03; subject to Irish High Court sanction and other steps; expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:16). The company expects 20 to 30 of annual cash savings from 2027 (Q3 release page:6). The plan to move to Texas did not pass in June 2026 (Q2 release page:5). Intellectual property transition steps are being evaluated for accounting and tax implications.

- NCS Multistage Holdings, Inc. acquired 2026-09-01 for total consideration of 128 (13 cash net of cash acquired, 1.0 million shares valued at 101, and 7 of assumed equity awards), with tangible assets acquired 150 and liabilities acquired 34 (Q3 10-Q page:15). The Q3 10-Q does not describe any debt acquired.
- Supplemental indenture of 2026-09-25 adding Weatherford International Holding LLC as co-issuer of the 2033 notes (Q3 10-Q page:10 and page:39).
### Consumer readiness
| Consumer | View | Evidence cited and limits |
| CP-1A | Sufficient with limits | Entity, perimeter, debt obligors and transaction facts above come from Q3 10-Q pages:10, 11, 15 and 16; limits are the unseen indentures and merger agreement. |
| CP-2 | Sufficient with limits | Statements, debt by instrument, liquidity and cash flow metrics above; limited by the company-defined EBITDA and no covenant headroom. |
| CP-5 | Sufficient with limits | Every figure is tied to a page locator in this handoff; split-table stitching and the release-sourced FY2025 adjusted EBITDA are the points to test. |

## Calculations
All inputs are reported figures from the cited pages, in US$ millions. Results are shown as calculated and rounded as stated. No result replaces a source-printed value.

1. Total debt. Current portion of long-term debt plus long-term debt. 2026-09-30: 264 plus 1,216 = 1,480 (Q3 10-Q page:3), equal to the release total debt (Q3 release page:15). 2025-12-31: 30 plus 1,455 = 1,485.
2. Debt composition check at 2026-09-30: 1,183 plus 234 plus 63 = 1,480 (Q3 10-Q page:9), where finance leases are 30 plus 33.
3. Net debt. Total debt less cash and cash equivalents less restricted cash. 2026-09-30: 1,480 less 1,161 less 37 = 282, equal to the company figure (Q3 release page:16).

4. Trailing twelve months adjusted EBITDA at 2026-09-30. FY2025 trailing figure 1,067 (Q1 release page:15) less nine months 2025 776 plus nine months 2026 710 = 1,001, equal to the company figure (Q3 release page:16). The Q3 reconciliation also ties: 153 plus 70 plus 4 plus 6 plus 6 plus 15 = 254 (operating income, depreciation and amortization, other charges, restructuring, redomestication, share-based compensation).

5. Leverage ratios. Total debt over trailing adjusted EBITDA: 1,485 / 1,067 = 1.39x (2025-12-31); 1,484 / 1,047 = 1.42x (2026-03-31); 1,480 / 1,016 = 1.46x (2026-06-30); 1,480 / 1,001 = 1.48x (2026-09-30). Net debt over the same: 443 / 1,067 = 0.42x; 434 / 1,047 = 0.41x; 343 / 1,016 = 0.34x; 282 / 1,001 = 0.28x. The net ratios equal the company-reported ratios in the releases (Q1 release page:15, Q2 release page:15, Q3 release page:16).

6. EBITDA before add-backs, trailing twelve months at 2026-09-30. Operating income plus depreciation and amortization: FY2025 756 plus 267 = 1,023; nine months 2025 557 plus 193 = 750; nine months 2026 383 plus 211 = 594. Trailing = 1,023 less 750 plus 594 = 867. The 70 gain on sale is in both the FY2025 and nine-month 2025 figures and cancels. Bridge to adjusted EBITDA: 1,001 less 867 = 134, equal to trailing share-based compensation 50 (38 less 26 plus 38) plus restructuring 35 (58 less 51 plus 28) plus redomestication 30 (none before 2026) plus other charges net 19 (18 less 19 plus 20) = 134. Total debt / 867 = 1.71x; net debt / 867 = 0.33x.

7. Trailing cash interest paid. FY2025 125 (10-K page:70). Q1 2026: 125 less 2 (Q1 2025) plus 1 (Q1 2026) = 124 (Q1 10-Q page:3). Q2 2026: 125 less 70 plus 55 = 110 (Q2 10-Q page:4). Q3 2026: 125 less 71 plus 57 = 111 (Q3 10-Q page:4). Interest cover = trailing adjusted EBITDA over trailing interest paid: 1,067 / 125 = 8.54x; 1,047 / 124 = 8.44x; 1,016 / 110 = 9.24x; 1,001 / 111 = 9.02x.

8. Undrawn committed facilities. Commitment 1,000 less borrowings 0 less financial letters of credit less performance letters of credit. 2025-12-31: 1,000 less 7 less 245 = 748. 2026-03-31: 1,000 less 7 less 257 = 736. 2026-06-30: 1,000 less 4 less 243 = 753. 2026-09-30: 1,000 less 1 less 233 = 766. Revolving portion available for cash borrowing, from the 10-K split, at 2026-09-30: 600 less 1 financial letter of credit = 599 (split not restated in the 10-Qs; assumes it is unchanged). Liquidity at 2026-09-30: 1,161 plus 766 = 1,927 (or 1,161 plus 599 = 1,760 on the cash-drawable basis). Cash net of the 164 stated as not immediately repatriable: 1,161 less 164 = 997; whether the Russian cash of 128 overlaps with the 164 is not stated.

9. Trailing flows at 2026-09-30. Revenue: 4,918 less 3,629 plus 3,400 = 4,689. Operating cash flow: 676 less 408 plus 503 = 771. Capital expenditures: 226 less 175 plus 141 = 192. Proceeds from disposition of assets: 16 less 11 plus 17 = 22. Company-definition adjusted free cash flow: 771 less 192 plus 22 = 601.

10. Cash flow before working capital items, nine months. 2026: 503 less 65 = 438. 2025: 408 less (116) = 524. Change 438 less 524 = (86), about 16 percent lower. The 65 and (116) are the release's working capital caption (Q3 release page:13); the components in the 10-Q (186, (19), (72), (7), (23)) sum to 65.

11. Illustrative pro forma for the announced redemption, not an evidenced result. Remove the 2030 notes carrying value of 234 from total debt (1,480 less 234 = 1,246) and 236 from cash and restricted cash (1,198 less 236 = 962) at 2026-09-30. Net debt 1,246 less 962 = 284 (the 2 difference is unamortized issuance cost and ignores accrued interest). Total debt / 1,001 = 1.24x. Completion of the redemption is not evidenced in the sources.

12. Shareholder distributions, nine months 2026: dividends 59 plus repurchases 54 = 113, equal to the release figure (Q3 release page:5). Adjusted free cash flow 379 less 113 = 266 before debt repayment of 25 and other financing items.
## Gaps

## Next module

Proceed to CP-1A with this handoff: entity and obligor roles, debt stack, the pending redomestication, the NCS Multistage acquisition and the October 2026 redemption are the transaction facts to carry, each with the locators above. CP-2 should use the leverage, interest cover, liquidity and cash flow quality conclusions with their definition limits, and show covenant headroom as Not supplied. CP-5 should test the stitched tables, the trailing-period arithmetic and the release-sourced FY2025 adjusted EBITDA. If the executed credit agreement or any filing after 2026-10-21 and before the cutoff becomes available, add it as a separate source and revisit covenant headroom and the redemption status.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Weatherford is a diversified oilfield services group with no sponsor and no disclosed controlling holder. Its credit risk is cyclical demand, Middle East disruption, customer concentration and a pending corporate move, not owner behaviour. | Medium | Governing debt documents, ownership detail and the redomestication terms are not supplied, so creditor protections and structural effects cannot be assessed. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Revenue comes from three well-lifecycle segments across about 75 countries, and most revenue is international. | Diversification limits single-market risk, but earnings follow customer spending and regional disruption. | Medium |

| The Iran Conflict has cut Middle East, North Africa and Asia revenue in 2026 while higher oil prices have not lifted group revenue. | Near-term earnings and cash conversion depend on the pace of regional recovery. | Medium |
| A Mexican customer with a history of late payment is a large share of receivables, and Russia holds cash and assets. | Collection delays and restricted cash can reduce usable liquidity. | Medium |

| Debt was refinanced in 2025, the acquisition of NCS Multistage was paid mostly in shares, and the remaining 2030 notes were called in October 2026. | Debt service and refinancing pressure eased; the effect of the pending corporate move on obligors is not described. | Medium |

| No sponsor or extraction behaviour is documented; payouts to shareholders continued during 2026 from operating cash flow. | Owner-driven leakage is not evidenced, though indenture limits on payouts are not visible. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

Weatherford is a listed, widely held global oilfield services group that sells equipment and services across the well lifecycle through three segments: Drilling and Evaluation, Well Construction and Completions, and Production and Intervention. The consolidated reporting entity is Weatherford International plc, an Irish public limited company with principal executive offices in Houston, Texas. The sources disclose no sponsor, no controlling shareholder and no dividend recapitalisation history, so creditor control rests on the debt documents rather than on an owner. The creditor-relevant story in the sources is operating and structural. First, demand follows customer capital spending and rig activity, and in 2026 the Iran Conflict has cut regional activity even as oil prices were higher; revenue has fallen while margins were held by cost action. Second, receivable and cash concentration (a Mexican customer with late payments, Russian operations holding cash, cash that cannot be repatriated freely) can slow conversion of earnings to usable liquidity. Third, the capital structure was reshaped in the last twelve months: a 2025 refinancing into 6.75% notes due 2033, an equity-funded acquisition of NCS Multistage Holdings, Inc. that closed on 2026-09-01, an announced redemption of the remaining 8.625% notes due 2030 from cash, and a pending redomestication of the parent from Ireland to Delaware that shareholders approved on 2026-09-03 and that awaits court sanction. The terms of the redomestication that bear on lenders (guarantors, collateral, the intellectual property transition) are not described in the sources. Governance evidence is limited to documented actions: refinancing and redemption that reduce interest cost, continued dividends and buybacks funded from operating cash flow, and co-issuer additions on the notes whose purpose is not explained. This supports a Supportive to Neutral reading of issuer-level behaviour, with Insufficient Information on legal capacity. The view carries Medium confidence because filings control the facts, but the executed credit agreement, the indentures and the proxy statement that would show ownership are not in the pack.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

New debt issues: the sources show one new bond issue in the last two years and none in 2026. On 2025-10-06 Weatherford International Ltd. issued 6.75% senior notes due 2033-10-15 (principal 1.2 billion as printed); the tender offer and redemption of most of the 8.625% senior notes due 2030 used the proceeds of that issue and cash on hand, and the company recorded a 39 loss on extinguishment and redemption premium (10-K page:84 and page:44; Documentary Fact). The mechanism for a creditor is lower coupon and a maturity pushed from 2030 to 2033 on most of the bond debt, with the stub of the 2030 notes (principal about 236) left outstanding until the October 2026 call. On 2025-09-18 the credit agreement was amended to raise the commitment from 720 to 1 billion with an accordion to 1.15 billion and to extend its maturity (10-K page:55; Documentary Fact); the amendment text is not supplied. No new borrowing is reported in the nine months to 2026-09-30 (CP-1 cash flow table; Q3 10-Q page:3 and page:4).

Acquisition: on 2026-05-31 Weatherford signed a definitive merger agreement to acquire NCS Multistage Holdings, Inc. for shares or a mix of shares and cash, subject to proration (Q2 10-Q page:14), and it closed on 2026-09-01 for total consideration of 128, made up of 13 cash net of cash acquired, 1.0 million ordinary shares valued at 101 and 7 for assumed equity awards (Q3 10-Q page:15; Documentary Fact). The acquired business brought tangible assets of 150, intangible assets and goodwill of 46 and liabilities of 34, plus 34 of noncontrolling interest (page:15). Management states that it expects "at least $15 million of cost synergies upon closing and integration" (Q2 release page:2; Management Language, not adopted). Mechanism: because most consideration was shares and assumed awards, the deal added little cash outflow or debt, so leverage effects are limited, but the 10-Q does not say whether NCS carried debt, and integration risk and cost remain. Appetite for further acquisitions is not inferred from one deal. The Q3 10-Q records that Advent-NCS Acquisition Limited Partnership, NCS's largest shareholder, received 357,159 shares, resold under a registered prospectus supplement (page:38); this is not a control position.

Redomestication: the first proposal (Ireland to Texas, announced 2026-04-02) received over 60% support but not the 75% needed and failed in June 2026 (Q1 10-Q page:12; Q2 release page:5). An updated proposal to redomesticate to Delaware was approved by shareholders on 2026-09-03 and is subject to sanction by the High Court of Ireland and other steps, with completion expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:16). Management expects annual cash savings of 20 to 30 from 2027 (Q3 release page:6; Management Language). Related restructuring activities, including the planned intellectual property transition, are "being evaluated for their potential accounting and tax implications" (Q3 10-Q page:16). Creditor mechanism: a change of parent and a transfer of intellectual property can alter which entities hold assets, who guarantees the debt and how the collateral is arranged, and whether credit agreement or indenture conditions apply. The sources do not describe any of those effects, so the lender impact is Insufficient Information and the pending status must be carried into every consumer. The 2026-09-25 supplemental indenture adding Weatherford International Holding LLC as co-issuer of the 2033 notes and releasing its guarantee (Q3 10-Q page:10 and page:39) may be a step in this reorganisation, but the sources do not say so and this is not inferred.

Debt events after the period: on 2026-10-20 the company issued notice to redeem all remaining 8.625% notes due 2030 (about 236 principal) at 100% plus accrued interest, expected on 2026-10-30 and funded from cash on hand; it expects to cut annualized cash interest by about 20 (Q3 10-Q page:16; Q3 release page:5). This is a subsequent event after the 2026-09-30 balance sheet, announced and expected before the cutoff but not confirmed as completed in any source. The CP-1 handoff holds the leverage and liquidity figures before and after this event. Because the facility's early maturity trigger refers to more than 200 of the 2030 notes outstanding (Q3 10-Q page:11), completing the redemption would remove that trigger (Analyst Interpretation).

Dividends: a quarterly dividend of 0.275 per share was declared on 2026-10-15, payable 2026-12-03 to holders of record on 2026-11-06 (Q3 10-Q page:15). The record date is after the cutoff and is a future term.

### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability. Evidence: revenue for nine months 2026 fell from 3,629 to 3,400 while rig counts and oil prices were higher (Q3 10-Q pages:2, 18, 19). Risk mechanic: the Iran Conflict removed regional activity in Middle East, North Africa and Asia, the group's largest region (10-K page:81; Q3 10-Q page:20), so revenue is driven by a regional shock and not by commodity prices alone; management expects recovery to be gradual and uncertain (Q3 10-Q page:29, Management Language). Credit implication: coverage and leverage metrics in CP-1 are exposed to a further or longer disruption; the timing of recovery is the key uncertainty. Counter-evidence: three segments and about 75 countries diversify the base, and sequential Q3 2026 revenue rose in North America and Latin America (Q3 release page:7, Documentary Fact).

2. Margin and cash flow risk. Evidence: cost of products and services was 69% of revenue in FY2025 against 65% as fixed costs fell more slowly than revenue (10-K page:42); nine-month operating income fell from 557 to 383 (Q3 10-Q page:2). Risk mechanic: fixed cost leverage cuts margins when volume falls; cost action (restructuring of 28) offsets only partly. Credit implication: free cash flow conversion shown in CP-1 depends on working capital release and cost savings that may not repeat.

3. Concentration risk. Evidence: the largest Mexican customer was 24% of receivables at 2025-12-31 and 14% at 2026-09-30 with a late payment history (10-K page:21; Q3 10-Q page:32); Russian operations held cash of 128 and 164 of cash cannot be immediately repatriated (Q3 10-Q pages:19, 31). Risk mechanic: slow collection raises working capital and factoring need; sanctions and exchange controls trap cash. Credit implication: usable liquidity is lower than headline cash; monitor receivable days and trapped cash. No logged conflict counters this translation.

4. Sponsor alignment and structure. Evidence: no sponsor, no disclosed controlling holder, shareholder payouts covered by free cash flow, co-issuer changes unexplained, redomestication pending (see the governance table). Risk mechanic: creditor protection rests on documents not supplied and on management decisions about obligors and collateral during the corporate move. Credit implication: monitor the closing steps, any guarantor or collateral change and the indenture covenant limits on payouts before relying on structure. The dated sequence conflict on the redomestication counters any reading of a fixed plan.

5. Key uncertainties. Middle East recovery timing; redomestication terms and completion; completion of the October 2026 redemption; NCS integration and any acquired debt; covenant headroom (not reported). Credit implication: Medium confidence overall.
